items.title: Rape-murder accused killed in police encounter; fourth case in West Bengal since BJP came to power
points: This image is used for representational purpose only. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto A man accused of raping and murdering a minor in West Bengal’s Uttar Dinajpur was shot dead by police, officials said on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Dilip Roy, the accused, was killed in the early hours of Monday (November 9, 2026) when the police attempted to arrest him.
This marks the fourth ‘encounter’ death in the State since the BJP government came to power in May 2026.
The accused, Dilip Roy, allegedly opened fire at a police team conducting a raid to arrest him at a village in Raiganj late on Sunday (November 8, 2026) night, they said.
He was taken to Raiganj Medical College and Hospital, where he was declared dead, a police official said.
Police had been on the lookout for Roy for four days following the recovery of the girl’s decomposed, unclothed body from a forest near the Kulik river on Friday (November 6, 2026).

items.title: Renault Duster 1.3 Turbo Petrol MPFi Planned – Lower Price Up To Rs 1.5 Lakh
points: That is what Renault seems to be fixing now with a new version of Duster powered by a low-cost 1.3L MPFI Turbo Petrol engine.
Currently, Duster is offered with a 1.0L Turbo Petrol engine and a 1.3L TGDI Turbo Petrol engine along with the 1.8L Hybrid powertrain.
With the 1.3L MPFI Turbo Petrol, Renault might increase the appeal of Duster to the mainstream and boost sales.
Renault knows this by now and the company seems to be working on a simpler and low-cost 1.3L MPFI Turbo Petrol engine option as opposed to the more powerful TGDI 1.3L Petrol engine option.
This MPFI Turbo Petrol engine option is not likely to replace the more performant 1.3L TGDI Turbo Petrol engine, but sell alongside it in a multi-powertrain strategy.
The 1.3L TGDI Turbo Petrol engine makes 163 bhp and 280 Nm.
This more affordable and less sophisticated 1.3L MPFI Turbo Petrol engine might develop around 140 bhp and 250 Nm, which are still quite respectable from a 1.3L 4-cylinder displacement stand point.

items.title: Apple Plans to Bring Autonomous Capabilities to Siri AI, Overhaul iOS 28 Approach: Report
points: Apple plans to turn Siri AI into an autonomous agent that will be able to take more actions on a user's behalf.
The iPhone maker reportedly wants to bring similar capabilities to the AI assistant as OpenAI’s Dots, Meta’s Muse, and Grok from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI.
OpenAI, Meta, and AI labs position their respective AI agents as an “AI companion” that can run in the background and take actions for the user when required.
Users can also hand over tasks, allowing the AI agents to do repetitive and monotonous tasks for the user.
Apart from this, the report highlights that Apple has overhauled its development strategy for its next-generation iOS and iPadOS updates.
The company has split its OS development into three stages, namely M1, M2, and M3, with each stage spanning eight weeks.
The M1 stage is divided into two four-week sprints.

items.title: Parliament’s Monsoon session remains unprorogued for record 88 days
points: A view of the Parliament building in New Delhi. | Photo Credit: The Hindu Parliament's Monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 88 days since both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13, breaking the previous record of 87 days in 2008.
As of Monday (November 9, 2026) morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session.
An extended or special sitting of Parliament within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, whereas convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.
This has added significance as a similar Constitution Amendment Bill had failed to secure the required numbers in the Lok Sabha during a special sitting of the Budget session on April 17.
The mere fact that a House remains unprorogued for an extended period does not, by itself, amount to any constitutional or procedural impropriety.

items.title: Delhi struggles with enforcement, violations of time, ‘green’ firecracker curbs worsen pollution
points: Despite the Supreme Court allowing green firecrackers in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) between 6am and 7am and 8pm and 10pm for two days ahead of Diwali, fireworks continued well past midnight when a complete ban took effect.

Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at consulting firm Envirocatalysts, said pollution levels began showing the impact of firecrackers even before Diwali night, with sulphur dioxide (SO2), a tell-tale indicator of firecracker emissions, rising sharply…
Green firecrackers are meant to emit only about 30% less than conventional ones, and 30% less of a very large amount is still a very large amount.

Dahiya said hourly, city-wide PM2.5 levels on Diwali night peaked at nearly 600 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³) around 1am, as per Central Pollution Control Board data, over 10 times the 24-hour standard of 60 µg/m³.
The court expected green firecrackers to cut PM2.5 emissions by at least 25-30%.
CSIR-NEERI claims these modifications cut emissions by 30-35% compared to traditional firecrackers.

items.title: Air of Deepavali celebrations lingers in Hyderabad with AQI remaining at hazardous levels

The data was sourced from publicly available pollution monitors as the Telangana Pollution Control Board monitors were out of order as the air pollution was rising.

The high AQI recordings were almost evenly spread through the city as a 20 degree celsius wind blew from the north-eastern direction.
The air pollution hit a peak at 9.30 p.m. before slowly dropping down through the night.
At 11.30 p.m. when the average AQI in Hyderabad was 442, Serilingampally recorded a high of 666.

points: Taiwanese shares rallied after authorities unveiled measures to restore investor confidence following the longest selling streak since 2022 amid a global AI stock rout.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and MediaTek Inc. led the gains, rising at least 5% each.

The Financial Supervisory Commission said after Friday’s market close that it will cap the volume of intraday short-sale orders for borrowed securities at 3% of a stock’s average daily trading volume over the preceding 30 days.
The financial regulator will also raise the minimum margin requirement for short-selling activities to 130% from 90%.

As part of the new system, all Pre-University (PU) colleges across Karnataka will follow a common examination timetable.
The question papers will be prepared at the state level and sent digitally to the respective colleges on the day of the examination.
The examinations will continue to be conducted under the supervision of the Department of School Education (Pre-University).
Under the revised arrangement, question papers for the 2027 annual examinations will be prepared centrally by KSEAB instead of being set separately at the college level.

items.title: Karnataka tests petrol samples at 67 locations over ethanol blending complaints: CM Shivakumar
points: Shivakumar said his government was taking the complaints seriously and questioned the silence of BJP and JD(S) leaders on the issue. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Karnataka Chief Minister D.

Shivakumar on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said petrol samples had been collected and tested at 67 locations across the state following complaints that increased ethanol blending was affecting vehicle engine performance.
Speaking to reporters in Bengaluru, Mr. Shivakumar said, “The government has taken serious note of complaints regarding 31.5 per cent ethanol being blended into petrol.
According to the CM, inspections had been carried out not only at petrol pumps but also at the stages of ethanol blending and distribution.
